vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: memclaw
Version: 0.9.14

The MemClaw skill bundle is a semantic memory system for OpenClaw that manages conversation history through a tiered retrieval system (L0/L1/L2). The tools provided (cortex_search, cortex_recall, cortex_add_memory, cortex_migrate, etc.) are clearly aligned with the stated purpose of enhancing memory management. File access is restricted to the application's own workspace (~/.openclaw/workspace), and the documentation explicitly disclaims data exfiltration or unauthorized API key transmission. No malicious code patterns, obfuscation, or harmful prompt-injection instructions were found.

llm.summary: The SKILL.md and tool docs are internally consistent with a local three-tier semantic memory plugin that reads and writes OpenClaw workspace files and uses whatever LLM/embedding provider is configured; there are no unexpected binaries, env vars, or install actions declared.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (MemClaw, L0/L1/L2 memory) match the instructions and tool set (cortex_search, cortex_recall, cortex_add_memory, etc.). Required resources (local memory files, OpenClaw settings) are appropriate for a memory plugin and nothing unrelated (e.g., cloud provider credentials or unrelated system services) is requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions explicitly read OpenClaw memory files (~/ .openclaw/workspace/memory/ and MEMORY.md) during migration and ask you to edit openclaw.json/plugin config. That access is expected for migration and operation, but it does mean the plugin will touch your workspace and OpenClaw configuration files — review/backup those before running migration or maintenance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are included (instruction-only). This minimizes risk because nothing is downloaded or written by an installer as part of skill installation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, which is consistent with relying on OpenClaw's existing configuration for LLM/embedding providers. SKILL.md does say it will not transmit API keys except to your configured provider — therefore the plugin will implicitly rely on provider credentials stored in OpenClaw config. Users should confirm where those keys live and be comfortable with the plugin accessing them via OpenClaw.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable (defaults). It mentions scheduled maintenance (cron) as a typical setup step, but the skill itself declares no mechanism to create persistent system-level services or modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its stated purpose, but before you enable it: (1) Verify the upstream project links in SKILL.md (the raw GitHub URLs) to ensure they point to the expected open-source repository and not a spoofed location. (2) Backup your OpenClaw workspace/memory files before running cortex_migrate or maintenance. (3) Confirm where your LLM/embedding provider credentials are stored in OpenClaw (openclaw.json or UI) and that you are comfortable allowing the memory plugin to use those provider settings; the skill claims all processing is local but will call whatever embedding/LLM provider you configure. (4) If you want higher assurance, ask the publisher for the plugin code or an install script to review (none was included here). If any of these checks fail or the repository is unverified, treat the skill cautiously.
